tldr: WebPilot is a multi-agent system that combines global and local Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)-inspired optimization strategies to enable autonomous agents to execute complex web tasks with human-like adaptability and strategic exploration.
contributions: WebPilot, an autonomous multi-agent system combining global and local MCTS-inspired optimization strategies for human-like flexibility in exploration, adaptation, and decision-making
A Hierarchical Reflection Mechanism incorporating Strategic Reflection in Global Optimization and Tactical Reflection in Local Optimization
A novel Granular Bifaceted Self-Reward Mechanism integrating action effectiveness with goal-oriented potential for more precise assessments in dynamic environments
SOTA performance on WebArena and MiniWoB++ benchmarks
methods: WebPilot employs a dual optimization strategy grounded in MCTS. The Global Optimization phase uses Hierarchical Task Decomposition (HTD) via a Planner to break complex tasks into manageable subtasks, and Reflective Task Adjustment (RTA) where a Controller assesses subtask completeness and generates strategic reflections to refine the high-level plan based on new observations, while an Extractor gathers essential information. The Local Optimization phase executes each subtask using a tailored MCTS with four stages: Goal-Oriented Selection (GOS) modifies the PUCT formula to manage vast action spaces; Reflection-Enhanced Node Expansion (RENE) integrates real-time feedback for tactical refinement; Dynamic Evaluation and Simulation (DES) assesses actions with one-step forward simulations; and Maximal Value Backpropagation (MVB) prioritizes paths based on maximum future rewards. Multiple specialized agents (Planner, Controller, Extractor, Explorer, Verifier, Appraiser) coordinate throughout.
results: WebPilot achieves a 37.2% success rate on WebArena with GPT-4, surpassing the SOTA method SteP. It demonstrates a 93% relative increase in success rate over concurrent tree-based methods (Koh et al. 2024) on WebArena. Even with GPT-3.5, WebPilot achieves a 29.1% success rate, remaining competitive with GPT-4-based SOTA methods. Experiments were conducted on both WebArena and MiniWoB++.
limitations: The paper notes that classical MCTS struggles with vast action spaces, unpredictable state transitions, and incomplete information in web tasks, and that existing reward mechanisms either rely on direct environment rewards (impractical for real-world tasks) or use overly simplistic scoring systems failing to capture nuanced, evolving web environments. The approach depends on LLM intuition quality for initial node value estimation. No explicit ablation numbers for individual components are provided in the given text excerpt.
